svg.title: Prithvi Raghu: research and selected work
svg.desc: I research quantum machine learning and scientific computing. Open to research collaborations. I study quantum circuits for learning, games and option pricing. I also model HF propagation for emitter geolocation. Quantum games (QHD): restricted GHZ equilibria admit unrestricted deviations, with compact payoff evaluation and recorded IBM Heron experiments in a co-authored manuscript. 7 players in one quantum game, run on real IBM quantum hardware. Quantum ML (FQCNN): coherent-pooling equivalence and four-task simulator benchmarks, with classical-baseline comparisons documented in a co-authored manuscript. 10 qubits classify 28 × 28 images. Option pricing (QOP): Asian-basket encodings trade qubits against gate count, with reproducible logical-resource comparisons and a manuscript draft. 50× fewer qubits than the arithmetic design, at 3.1× the gates. HF geolocation: a two-pass geolocation pipeline and Gaussian-process correction, evaluated on simulated emitter geometry with explicit limitations. 25% lower mean error, 103 to 77 km.
